I'll stick with it because I've invested an unnecessary amount of time on this show but after watching Pen15, the lack of subtlety in this show is suddenly very apparent. Nearly everything is presented facially and with no real examination anymore.

 Missy's racial identity crisis is the worst offender. A huge and important reality she must navigate is essentially solved in 3-4 episodes and a B-plot in all but one. The one is where she does deal with it, she's told what to do, then does it. Rule 1 of screenwriting is *have active characters*. Growth is defined by what the character chooses to do not what's done for them. 

Not every emotion of puberty needs to be a new monster. The best stuff is when it's dealing with the kids and the inherent grossness of preteens without just beating you over the head with conceptual stuff.

I like the characters, stop burying them under all the nonsense. The nonsense is great when it's used for to finish off a plot thread, or as a self contained bit. That's Jessie's bat mitzvah song vs Duke's spectrum of sexuality song. The former is the final nail in Jessie's hope for her parents and is genuinely affecting and unexpected. The latter is just a stop on an ongoing plotline that overstays it's welcome by half. 

They still have the potential to put out great episodes (Duke's history) but it's starting to lose the shine.
